title: Correctness of an AND or OR gadget
statement: Let $n,K$ be natural numbers, let $k$ be an AND or OR gate kind, and let $g$ be the gate with kind $k$ and argument list $args$. Suppose the existing gate list $gs$ is acyclic, every argument index is less than $n+|gs|$, and $|args|\le K$. Applying the binarization construction to $g$ and $gs$ yields a gate list and output vertex that extend $gs$ and form an acyclic circuit; the output vertex is less than $n$ plus the resulting list length and computes $g$ on the values produced by $gs$ for every Boolean input assignment. The resulting list has length at most $|gs|+|args|+2$, the output depth is at most $\lceil\log_2 K\rceil+1$ plus the maximum depth among the argument vertices in $gs$ (with empty maximum $0$), and every added gate is well formed with at most two arguments.
hypotheses_covered: Argument list $args$ and existing gate list $gs$
Every argument index is less than $n+|gs|$
